scenario.title: Ambiguous: 'make links safer and show who is clicking'
scenario.requirement:
Our short links need to be safer, and marketing wants to see who is clicking them.
Please get this done quickly without slowing redirects down.

design.comment: Security team: denylisted domains must also stop EXISTING links, not only new ones.

content.problem_statement: Reduce abuse of the shortener as a vector for harmful destinations, and give marketing audience analytics - without identifying individuals and without adding latency to redirects.
functional: Reject creation of links whose destination domain (or a parent domain) is on an operator-managed denylist
Stats report unique visitors in addition to total clicks
Visitor identity is pseudonymous: keyed, daily-rotating hash; the raw IP address is never stored
Visitor hashes are purged after the retention window
non_functional: Redirect path: no new network calls; one in-process HMAC; no extra queries
Privacy: data minimisation, purpose limitation (aggregate analytics), retention <= policy maximum

acceptance_criteria.text: Creating a link to a denylisted domain or any of its subdomains returns 422
Stats include unique_visitors (distinct visitors per day)
The raw client IP never reaches storage
Visitor hash is keyed (secret) and rotates daily
Visitor hashes older than the retention window are purged; click counts remain
Existing behaviour is unchanged for links and clients (regression)

content.title: Destination denylist + privacy-preserving visitor analytics
content.approach: Denylist is configuration (SHORTENER_BLOCKED_DOMAINS) checked in URL validation with parent-domain matching. Unique visitors are counted from a keyed HMAC of day|ip|user-agent stored in a new nullable clicks.visitor_hash column (migration v2); the raw IP exists only in memory for the request. A retention job nulls hashes older than the window while keeping click counts.
api_changes: GET /{code}: 410 when the destination is denylisted

data_handling.hashing: HMAC-SHA256(server secret, day|ip|user-agent), truncated to 128 bits
data_handling.rotation: day is part of the hash input, so visitors cannot be linked across days
data_handling.purpose: aggregate unique-visitor counts for marketing; no individual profiles or exports

tasks.title: Enforce denylist on redirect for existing links
Service: keyed daily visitor hash, retention purge
API: pass client IP to service, expose unique_visitors

alternatives_considered.decision: Aggregate unique visitors from a pseudonymous daily hash
alternatives_considered.why: Answers the marketing question (reach) without processing identities; keeps the change inside privacy policy.
rejected: Store raw IPs (personal data; needs legal basis, DPIA, access controls)

alternatives_considered.decision: HMAC-SHA256 with a server secret, day in the input
alternatives_considered.why: Unkeyed hashes of IPv4 are trivially brute-forced; the day component prevents cross-day tracking.

alternatives_considered.decision: Operator-managed config list with parent-domain matching
alternatives_considered.why: No new network dependency on the redirect path; deterministic; feeds can populate it later.
rejected: Live threat-intel API call per redirect (latency + availability coupling)

risks.risk: Denylist is only as good as its curation
risks.mitigation: follow-up: scheduled sync from a threat-intel feed

risks.risk: Random default secret makes unique counts restart-dependent
risks.mitigation: SHORTENER_VISITOR_SECRET documented as required in production

risks.risk: Unique visitors undercount users behind shared NAT
risks.mitigation: user agent is part of the hash; documented as an estimate

content.rollback_plan: Redeploy the previous version. Migration v2 only adds a nullable column, so old code runs unchanged; optionally run UPDATE clicks SET visitor_hash = NULL to drop pseudonymous data.
